holidays.name: National Gummi Bear Day
holidays.description: Celebrate the bouncy, chewy, fruity little bears that have been delighting candy lovers for generations. Sort them by color, bite off the heads first, or freeze them for a different texture. Today they all get eaten anyway.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance created to celebrate the gummy candy. The treat itself goes back to Germany in the early 1920s, when confectioner Hans Riegel of Haribo made a chewy fruit-gum bear called the Dancing Bear.
holidays.funFact: Haribo's name is a mash-up of its founder's name and hometown: HAns RIegel, BOnn. The original Dancing Bear was taller and slimmer than the squat gummi bears we know today.

holidays.name: National Tell A Story Day
holidays.description: Today is for dusting off your best tales, whether that's a family legend, a childhood mishap, or a totally embellished fish story. Gather some friends, swap stories, and let the details grow a little taller with each telling.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It celebrates storytelling, one of humanity's oldest art forms.
holidays.funFact: Researchers who study storytelling say that listeners' brains can sync up with the storyteller's. That may be why a good tale around a campfire feels so magical.

holidays.name: World Tapir Day
holidays.description: This day is a shout-out to the tapir, an odd and lovable mix of a pig, an anteater, and an elephant. It shines a light on the four tapir species and the habitat loss that threatens them.
holidays.origin: Conservationists established World Tapir Day to raise awareness of tapirs and the efforts to protect them and their forest and grassland homes in Central and South America and Southeast Asia.
holidays.funFact: Baby tapirs are born with white stripes and spots that look like a watermelon rind. The pattern camouflages them in dappled forest light and fades as they grow.
